newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer ahead of option expiry.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer ahead of option expiry.

text.p: Gold prices held on to positive moves recorded in New York and the Far East markets but professionals expect little drama on Monday morning ahead of the over the counter option expiry on Tuesday.
"The expiry is a big issue for the market. There will not be much movement ahead of it, and recently after expiries prices have tended to drift down," one dealer said.
Dealers said the options closest to the money for tomorrow's expiry were at $325.00 with interest at $320.00 and $330.00.

Gold fixed at $325.40 per ounce up from $324.10 on Friday afternoon and a close then of $323.80/$324.30. New York had closed firmer on Friday and a weaker yen encouraged investor buying of gold in Tokyo.
But Hong Kong closed off its highs despite short covering from Tokyo, Australia and later in its trading day, European dealers.

Dealer said gold's prospects on the upside were fairly limited medium term now that the market had got back to the levels it held before a news of a 167-tonne sale from the Australian central bank plunged it to 12-year lows.
The announcement on July 3 sent gold to $314.00 in a couple of days as market sentiment froze.
"Gold tried on Friday for the third time to reach $328/$329 but failed at ($326/$327) resistance," one dealer said.
He added Australian producers were selling into strength at $328-$329 which was limiting the upside potential.
"There is no real trend in gold. It is basically in a $320-$328 range with initial support at $324," one dealer said.
Above the range, $332/$333 was a more formidable obstacle representing a technically significant 40 percent retracement and below the range a breach could target $314.00.
Platinum was a couple of dollars firmer as nerves continued to jangle over the availability of delayed Russian exports to Japan and the European dealer market.
But one analyst countered, "As they have been producing and not exporting since December, there is every reason to think they actually have supplies."
Platinum was indicated at $424.50/$427.50, up $2.00 and still commanding lease rates of over 30 percent for a month.
Palladium was $3.50 firmer at $202.50/$205.50 after an investor-led surge in Tokyo, and silver was four cents up at $4.35/$4.37.
